rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take ‘from its like’ to mean a challenge to produce something like the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: قال بعضهم: (من مثله): من مثل القرآن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others understand the challenge as producing a sura from a human like Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم (من مثله) من بشر مثله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses are those whose obedience the challengers invoke and whose help they hope to enlist in producing a comparable sura.
rows.anchor: أي ادعوا من استدعيتم طاعته ورجوتم معونته في الإتيان بسورة من مثله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning follows proof of divine unity and prophethood: they are threatened if they still refuse belief after the proof is established.
rows.anchor: قيل لهم هذا بعد أن ثبت عليهم أمر التوحيد وأمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فوعدوا بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam makes the future action carry a past sense, so the verb is jussive.
rows.anchor: لم أحدثت في الفعل المستقبل معنى المضى فجزمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Particles take inflectional effects proportionate to their meaning; lan and its clause are accusative because أن with its clause functions like a noun, unlike lam’s jussive clause.
rows.anchor: وكل حرف لزم الفعل فأحدث فيه معنى فله فيه من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is described through the most painful thing people know, conveying that divine punishment is among the severest kinds they know.
rows.anchor: لا شيء في الدنيا أبلغ فيما يؤلم من النار، فقيل لهم إن عذاب الله من أشد الأجناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The stones are said to be stones of sulfur.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن الحجارة هنا تفسيرها حجارة الكبريت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqūd means firewood, or anything used to kindle a fire.
rows.anchor: الوقود هو الحطب، وكل ما أوقد به فهو وقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun is normally pronounced with ḍamma, though fatḥa is also allowed; Arabic uses the pattern fuʿūl for a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقد روي وقدت النار وقودا وقبلت الشيء قبولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are told their reward after the preceding account of what awaits unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ذكر ذلك للمؤمنين، وما أعد لهم جزاء لتصديقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The position of أن is accusative: when bi is omitted, the verb governs the clause directly.
rows.anchor: فلما سقطت الباء أفضى الفعل إلى " أن " فنصبت.

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians allow the clause’s position to remain genitive after bi is omitted; جنات itself is accusative through أن.
rows.anchor: قال بعض النحويين إنه يجوز أن يكون موضع مثل هذا خفضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, janna means a garden and jannāt means gardens; these are promised to the God-fearing with delights for souls and eyes.
rows.anchor: والجنة في لغة العرب البستان، والجنات البساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their first lifeless state was as sperm, then they became living beings, died, were resurrected, and return to God after resurrection.
rows.anchor: فكونهم أمواتا أولا أنهم كانوا نطفا ثم جعلوا حيوانا ثم أميتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return is after resurrection; the cited descriptions say they hasten toward the caller and emerge swiftly from their graves.
rows.anchor: كما قال (مهطعين إلى الداع) أي مسرعين. وقوله، عز وجل (يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا). والأجداث القبور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa is an interrogative expressing astonishment, addressed to people and believers: marvel that these people disbelieve despite God’s established proof.
rows.anchor: وتأويل كيف أنها، استفهام في معنى التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means ‘you had been’; the wāw is circumstantial, with qad understood from context.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (وكنتم) وقد كنتم وهذه الواو للحال، وإضمار قد جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad may be omitted when the wording supplies evidence, as in the examples about constricted hearts and a shirt torn from behind.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله (أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم) (وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is the object: everything on earth is created as a benefit bestowed for you.
rows.anchor: موضع ما مفعول به وتأويله أن جميع ما في الأرض منعم به عليكم فهو لكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes provision of everything on earth as evidence for God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: وفيه قول آخر أن ذلكم دليل على توحيد الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some understand istawā ilā as intending or turning toward heaven, as a prince is said to turn toward a city.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان: قال بعضهم: (استوى إلى السماء)، عمد وقصد إلى السماء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as God’s command ascending to heaven.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل (أيضا) استوى أي صعد أمره إلى السماء وهذا قول ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-samāʾ has singular form but plural meaning, as shown by the phrase ‘made them seven heavens.’
rows.anchor: والسماء لفظها لفظ الواحد، ومعناها معنى الجمع. والدليل على ذلك قوله: (فسواهن سبع سماوات).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-samāʾ may itself be a plural, with singular forms samāh or samāwah and samāʾ used for the collective.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون السماء جمعا كما أن السماوات جمع كأن واحده سماة وسماوة وسماء للجميع.

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows a singular form such as al-samāʾ to denote a plural, as in ‘the dirham and dinar became numerous among people.’
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن الأخفش أن السماء جائز أن يكون واحدا يراد به الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word means a roof and more generally anything elevated; clouds are called sky because they are high.
rows.anchor: والسماء في اللغة السقف ويقال لكل ما ارتفع وعلا قد سما يسمو، وكل سقف، فهو سماء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls idh redundant; al-Zajjāj rejects this as reckless because idh is a noun meaning ‘time.’
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة " إذ " ههنا زائدة، وهذا إقدام من أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the creation of people and others, the passage links their creation to the time God told the angels He would place a successor on earth.
rows.anchor: والحجة في (إذ) أن الله تعالى ذكر خلق الناس وغيرهم، فكأنه قال ابتدأ خلقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about Adam and the angels’ prostration proves Muhammad’s prophethood to scriptural communities: Arabs did not know it, while scripture readers or revelation did.
rows.anchor: ففي إخبار النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - دليل على تثبيت رسالته إذ آتاهم بما ليس من علم العرب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A people called jinn lived on earth, corrupted it and shed blood; God sent angels to drive them away, and the angels then inhabited earth.
rows.anchor: روي أن خلقا يقال لهم الجان كانوا في الأرض فأفسدوا وسفكوا الدماء

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another account says God told the angels some descendants of Adam would shed blood and allowed their question to affirm that He knows the unseen.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: المعنى فيه غير هذا وهو أن الله عز وجل أعلم الملائكة أنه جاعل في الأرض خليفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels ask to learn the wisdom, not to object: they seek clarification of the truth if their expectation is correct.
rows.anchor: وتأويل استخبارهم هذا على جهة الاستعلام وجهة الحكمة، لا على الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported account, God gave the angels leave to ask about the matter.
rows.anchor: وأذن الله عز وجل للملائكة أن يسألوه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will test those the angels expect to obey, and through the test guide them.
rows.anchor: أي أبتلي من تظنون أنه يطيع فيهديه الابتلاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the hamza affirms making here and cites Jarīr’s ألستم as evidence for the form’s affirmative force.
rows.anchor: الألف ههنا إنما هي على إيجاب الجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safaka means to pour or spill something.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (يسفك) يصب، يقال سفك الشيء إذا صبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To glorify God with praise means to declare Him free of evil.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (نسبح بحمدك) نبرئك من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any act intended for God may be called tasbīḥ; completing prayer is one Arabic use of tasbīḥ.
rows.anchor: وكل من عمل عملا قصد به الله فقد سبح، يقال فرغت من تسبيحي أي من صلاتي

rows.speaker: سيبويه وغيره من النحويين
rows.claim: Sībawayh and other grammarians gloss subḥān Allāh as declaring God free of evil and exalting Him above it.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه وغيره من النحويين: إن معنى سبحان الله: براءة الله من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses the word سبحان to mean disavowal of ʿAlqama and his boasting.
rows.anchor: المعنى البراءة منه ومن فخره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuqaddisu laka means purifying ourselves for God; the obedient person is purified, and Bayt al-Maqdis is the purified house or place of purification from sins.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (نقدس لك) أي نطهر أنفسنا لك، وكذلك من أطاعك نقدسه أي نطهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahratan means openly, with nothing hidden from view; the same usage describes openly committing sins without concealment.
rows.anchor: معنى (جهرة) غير مستتر عنا بشيء، يقال فلان يجاهر بالمعاصي أي لا يستتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣāʿiqa is what strikes people dead, and the Israelites died when it struck them.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (فأخذتكم الصاعقة) معنى الصاعقة ما يصعقون منه، أي يموتون، فأخذتهم الصاعقة فماتوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse’s statement that God raised them after their death proves the ṣāʿiqa killed them.
rows.anchor: الدليل على أنهم ماتوا قوله عز وجل: (ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون (56).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This worldly resurrection is likened to the man revived after a century and the people God told to die and then restored.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله تعالى: (فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه). ومثل قوله عز وجل: (فقال لهم الله موتوا ثم أحيأهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripturally corroborated reports of resurrection answer Arab polytheists who doubted resurrection and support Muhammad’s mission among Jews, Christians, and other scriptural communities.
rows.anchor: فأتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالأخبار عمن بعث بعد الموت في الدنيا مما توافقه عليه اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In هو محرم عليكم إخراجهم, the pronoun may refer back to the previously mentioned expulsion: expelling them is forbidden to you.
rows.anchor: جائز أن يكون إضمار الإخراج الذي تقدم ذكره. قال: (وتخرجون فريقا منكم من ديارهم) وهو محرم عليكم إخراجهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, هو may introduce the matter or report: their expulsion is forbidden, like ‘Say: He is God, One.’
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون للقصة، والحديث والخبر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For disgrace and evil one says khazā; for shyness or embarrassment one says khaziya yakhzī khazāya.
rows.anchor: يقال في الشر والسوء خزي الرجل خزيا، ويقال في الحياء خزي يخزي خزاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishments described as severe, great, or painful are two kinds apportioned according to sins.
rows.anchor: العذاب على ضربين، على " قدر المعاصي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning of a blazing fire entered only by the most wretched illustrates one punishment category.
rows.anchor: والدليل على ذلك قوله عز وجل: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى (14) لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى (15)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book given to Moses is the Torah.
rows.anchor: (ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب) يعني التوراة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God choosing someone for His mercy here means choosing whom He wills for prophethood.
rows.anchor: أي يختص بنبوته من يشاء من أخبر - عز وجل - أنه مختار.

rows.speaker: قراء
rows.claim: The text transmits three readings of the form: nunsihā, nansahā, and nunsāʾhā.
rows.anchor: في (ننسها) غير وجه قد قرئ به: أو ننسها، وننسها، وننسؤها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, naskh means abolishing one thing and putting another in its place, as the sun removes shade and replaces it.
rows.anchor: فأما النسخ في اللغة فإبطال شيء وإقامة آخر مقامه، العرب تقول نسخت الشمس الظل

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some lexicographers derive the phrase from forgetting, citing ‘You will recite, and you will not forget, except what God wills’; al-Zajjāj rejects this reading.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم، (أو ننسها) من النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That derivation cannot mean God wills to remove revelation: 17:86 says He would not will to take away what He revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لأن الله عز وجل: قد أنبأ النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في قوله (ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception in ‘you will not forget except what God wills’ can mean leaving something aside by choice or ordinary human forgetting followed by later recollection, not stripping the Prophet of revealed wisdom.
rows.anchor: أحدهما (فلا تنسى) أي لست تترك إلا ما شاء الله أن تترك، ويجوز أن يكون إلا ما شاء الله مما يلحق بالبشرية، ثم تذكر بعد

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another gloss takes it as ‘or leave it’; al-Zajjāj rejects أنسى for ‘leave’ and says it means God commands that the verse be left.
rows.anchor: وقيل في (أو ننسها) قول آخر وهو خطأ أيضا، قالوا أو نتركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation replaces a verse with another that cancels its ruling; leaving means believers stop a practice without a later abrogating verse, as with the test of emigrant women.
rows.anchor: أن النسخ يأتي في الكتاب في نسخ الآية بآية فتبطل الثانية العمل بالأولى. ومعنى الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading nunsāʾhā means ‘or defer it’; nasʾ in Arabic means delay, as in asking God to extend someone’s term.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ " أو ننسؤها " أراد نؤخرها. والنسء في اللغة التأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Better than it’ means better for you; completing the fast replaced the earlier permission to abstain for those able to fast.
rows.anchor: المعنى بخير منها لكم، (أو مثلها) فأما ما يؤتى فيه بخير من المنسوخ فتمام الصيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Or its like’ means a verse with equal reward; the replacement may be easier to follow and more readily accepted by people.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله (أو مثلها) أي نأتي بآية ثوابها كثواب التي قبلها، والفائدة في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The change of qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba illustrates an equally rewarded act whose command at that time was more fitting and drew Arabs and others toward Islam.
rows.anchor: وعدل بها عن القصد لبيت المقدس، فهذا - وإن كان السجود إلى سائر النواحي متساويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kutiba ʿalaykum means ‘it was prescribed for you.’
rows.anchor: معنى (كتب عليكم) فرض عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs held power over others, married into them without dowries, and demanded excessive blood revenge, killing a free person of the weaker group for a slave of their own.
rows.anchor: يقال إنه كان لقوم من العرب طول على آخرين فكانوا يتزوجون فيهم بغير مهور، ويطلبون بالدم أكثر من مقداره

words: فَمَنْ عُفِىَ لَهُۥ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَىْءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the victim’s kin waive execution and accept blood money from an intentional killer, the killer’s life is spared and compensation is due.
rows.anchor: أي من ترك له القتل ورضي منه بالدية - وهو قاتل متعمد للقتل عفى له بأن ترك له دمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities were prescribed only life for life in the Torah; this community was granted the easing of blood money when accepted.
rows.anchor: كما قال عز وجل: (وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس) أي في التوراة - فتفضل الله على هذه الأمة بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis puts proper pursuit of the blood money on the victim’s kin and gracious payment on the killer.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (فاتباع بالمعروف) على ضربين: جائز أن يكون فعلى صاحب الدم اتباع بالمعروف، أي المطالبة بالدية، وعلى القاتل أداء بإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, both proper pursuit and gracious payment are duties of the killer.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون الإتباع بالمعروف والأداء بإحسان جميعا على القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After receiving blood money, whoever transgresses by unjustly killing the killer is promised painful punishment; iʿtidāʾ means wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي بعد أخذ الدية، ومعنى اعتدى: ظلم، فوثب فقتل قاتل صاحبه بعد أخذ الدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative means ‘pursuit is due’; an accusative verbal noun would be possible outside the Qur’an, but nominative is better Arabic and the transmitted reading is binding.
rows.anchor: ورفع (فاتباع بالمعروف) على معنى فعليه اتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥayātun may be nominative as a subject, or as a subject related to لكم, meaning that life is established for you in retaliation; ulū al-albāb means people of reason.
rows.anchor: (حياة) رفع على ضربين: على الابتداء، وعلى لكم، كأنه قال وثبت لكم في القصاص حياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that killing brings execution restrains a would-be killer, saving the intended victim; it also preserves the killer’s life because he refrains and is not executed.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الحياة في القصاص أن الرجل - إذا علم أنه يقتل إن قتل - أمسك عن القتل ففي إمساكه عن القتل حياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second ‘prescribed for you’ omits the conjunction waw, which long discourse can leave understood; the sense is that both retaliation and bequest were prescribed.
rows.anchor: إذا طال استغنى عن العطف بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bequest requirement was abrogated by the inheritance verses in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ; Zajjāj explains its original wisdom because God prescribes with profound wisdom.
rows.anchor: هذا الفرض بإجماع نسخته آيات المواريث في سورة النساء وهذا مجمع عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original prescription meant that one who left wealth was to bequeath fairly to parents and relatives.
rows.anchor: فمعنى (كتب عليكم): فرض عليكم - إن ترك أحدكم مالا - الوصية (للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waṣiyya may be the passive subject in ‘the bequest was prescribed,’ or a nominative topic with li-l-wālidayn as predicate in the sense of a reported instruction.
rows.anchor: فرفع الوصية على ضربين، أحدهما على ما لم يسم فاعله، كأنه قال كتب عليكم الوصية للوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addressed favoritism toward distant outsiders for display and reputation by directing a fair bequest to parents and close relatives.
rows.anchor: وإنما أمروا بالوصية في ذلك الوقت لأنهم كانوا ربما جاوزوا بدفع المال إلى البعداء طلبا للرياء والسمعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not require making a will while death is actually present, when a person is occupied; it requires arranging it while still able, in anticipation of death.
rows.anchor: ليس هو إنه كتب عليه أن يوصي إذا حضره الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-maʿrūf means what a discerning person recognizes as free of bias and injustice.
rows.anchor: بالشيء الذي يعلم ذو التمييز أنه لا جنف فيه ولا جور

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say the bequest command remains for one third; al-Zajjāj rejects this as an obligatory command, since Muslims agree one may bequeath a third or leave it, and the verse’s prescription was abrogated.
rows.anchor: وأمر الوصية في الثلث باق، وهذا القول ليس بشي لأن إجماع المسلمين أن ثلث الرجل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaqqan is accusative as ‘that is truly required of you’; outside Qur’anic wording, nominative would also be grammatical.
rows.anchor: نصب على حق ذلك عليكم حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing a will, the person who changes it bears the sin, not a careful testator or the beneficiary.
rows.anchor: يعني فمن بدل أمر الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God heard the testator’s words and knows what the beneficiary does, for He knows the seen and unseen.
rows.anchor: أي قد سمع ما قاله الموصي، وعلم ما يفعله الموصى إليه، لأنه عز وجل عالم الغيب والشهادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading is used; accusative is also allowed but is less common.
rows.anchor: القراءة بالرفع ويجوز النصب، وهي قراءة ليست بالكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the nominative, three parses are possible: a fresh statement with an understood ‘fasting/days prescribed’; apposition to fasting in the passive; or an initial topic whose predicate is ‘in which the Qur’an was sent down.’
rows.anchor: ورفعه على ثلاثة أضرب: أحدها الاستئناف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative has two parses: apposition to ‘numbered days,’ or an exhortative command meaning ‘adhere to Ramadan.’
rows.anchor: ومن نصب شهر رمضان نصبه على وجهين، أحدهما أن يكون بدلا من أيام معدودات. والوجه الثاني على الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever is present rather than traveling must fast; the sick and travelers may make up the corresponding days later.
rows.anchor: ومعنى من شهد: من كان شاهدا غير مسافر فليصم، ومن كان مسافرا أو مريضا فقد جعل له أن يصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāsik are the acts of worship commanded during pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أي متعبداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the rites, Arabs stood between the mosque at Minā and the mountain, listing their fathers’ virtues and recalling their notable days.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب إذا قضت مناسكها، وقفت بين المسجد بمنى وبين الجبل فتعدد فضائل آبائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God redirects that remembrance to Himself and calls for more: declare His oneness and recount His blessings, since blessings attributed to ancestors come from God and merit thanks to Him.
rows.anchor: وأن يزيدوا على ذلك الذكر فيذكروا الله بتوحيده وتعديد نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashadda is in a genitive syntactic position but indeclinable on the afʿal pattern as an adjective; alternatively it is accusative under an understood ‘remember Him more intensely.’
rows.anchor: (أشد) في موضع خفض ولكنه لا يتصرف لأنه على مثال أفعل، وهو صفته، وإن شئت كان نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikran is an accusative specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: و (ذكرا) منصوب على التميز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ātinā is a pause point because it is a supplication; it means ‘give us in this world.’
rows.anchor: (آتنا) وقف لأنه دعاء، ومعناه أعطنا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are Arab polytheists who asked for worldly ease but sought no afterlife share because they did not believe in it.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء مشركو العرب كانوا يسألون التوسعة عليهم في الدنيا ولا يسألون حظا من الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalāq means an abundant share of good.
rows.anchor: يعني هؤلاء، والخلاق النصيب الوافر من الخير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those asking for good in both worlds are the believers.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء المؤمنون يسألون الحظ في الدنيا والآخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinā comes from waqā; the wāw drops as in yaqī, the connecting alif is no longer needed, and the yāʾ drops at pause (or, in Kufan analysis, because of jussive mood).
rows.anchor: والأصل في " قنا " او قينا - ولكن الواو سقطت كما سقطت من يقي، لأن الأصل " يوقي "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer means: make us protected from the punishment of the Fire.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أجعلنا موقين من عذاب النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine is the agreed case; by analogy, anything that acts like it is also called khamr and has the same prohibition.
rows.anchor: (الخمر) المجمع عليه، وقياس كل ما عمل عملها أن يقال له خمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr is named from covering: it applies to what veils a person, a woman’s veil, a prayer mat covering the face, and dough covered by fermentation.
rows.anchor: وتأويل الخمر في اللغة أنه كل ما ستر العقل، يقال لكل ما ستر الإنسان مق شجر وغيره خمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All intoxicants are khamr because they mix with and cover the intellect, whatever name they are given; drinkers are described as intoxicated or suffering a hangover.
rows.anchor: فهذا كله يدل على أن كل مسكر خمر وكل مسكر مخالط العقل ومغط عليه، وليس يقول أحد للشارب

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
rows.claim: After someone claimed a differently named intoxicant was lawful, Abū al-Aswad recognized it as wine’s kin; his poem says the two are siblings nurtured by the same mother.
rows.anchor: وقد لبس على ابي الأسود الدؤلي فقيل له: إن هذا المسكر الذي سموه بغير الخمر حلال

rows.speaker: قراء
rows.claim: A variant reading has kathīr (‘much’) in place of kabīr (‘great’) in the phrase about sin.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير في قوله عز وجل: (قل فيهما إثم كبير) وقرئت " كثير "

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say this verse only discouraged wine and gambling, with their prohibition made explicit later in al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: قال قوم زهد فيها في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others say the prohibition is already conveyed here and is clarified by the Book elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: لا بل تحرم بما بين ههنا مما دل عليه الكتاب في موضع آخر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question urges people to stop and rebukes them for not ceasing.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (فهل أنتم منتهون) التحضيض على الانتهاء والتفديد على ترك الانتهاء.
